title: Rẽ trái ở đâu?
summary: Ask "Where do I turn left?" with Rẽ trái ở đâu?, then use the notes below to understand likely replies and next steps.

sections.title: At a glance
sections.body: Rẽ trái ở đâu? answers the traveler question "Where do I turn left" in finding places, turns, distance, and walking directions. This is for when you are already on the route and need the next turn. Take the route one turn at a time. Its job is turning the problem into something the other person can point to, type, or mark on a map. Expect a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name; then use Explore next if the reply creates another small task.

sections.title: Break it down
sections.body: This pattern asks where a place or service is. Swap the first part to ask about another nearby stop.

sections.title: The standard way
sections.body: Start with Rẽ trái ở đâu? when "Where do I turn left" is the main thing you need understood. This is for when you are already on the route and need the next turn. It gives the other person room to answer with a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name. Show the map, address, or destination while you say it so the answer has a clear anchor.

sections.title: Why it matters
sections.body: Direction phrases turn a vague travel problem into a specific next step. For "Where do I turn left", the useful move is turning the problem into something the other person can point to, type, or mark on a map. If the answer is longer than a point or a place name, ask them to show it on your phone.

sections.title: Traveler insight
sections.body: In Directions & Navigation, locals often answer with a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name rather than a long explanation. That makes Rẽ trái ở đâu? strongest when you say it once, pause, and let the other person show the next step. Show the map, address, or destination while you say it so the answer has a clear anchor.

sections.title: When to use it
sections.body: This is for when you are already on the route and need the next turn. It fits finding places, turns, distance, and walking directions, especially when the next step is a point, short direction, nearby option, or counter name. If the answer is longer than a point or a place name, ask them to show it on your phone.

sections.title: Good to know
sections.body: If the answer is long, ask them to point or type it. Street directions can be hard to catch by ear.

sections.title: Local tip
sections.body: Show the map or address first, then ask the phrase. The answer is easier to understand when both of you see the same place.
